work.name: Université de Genève
work.summary: I recruited, assessed and supervised MCI patients, and trained their caregivers for a clinical research trial on the possible behavioral benefits during and after a 3-month long transcranial stimulation procedure. The stimulations, targeting the left angular gyrus, were performed at home by the caregivers while our team supervised the sessions remotely.

work.name: Université de Genève
work.summary: While I decided to interrupt my PhD, I was offered to continue and finish my work related to ASR implementation and experimental data analysis. During that period, I worked closely with a small team of two undergraduate research assistants who assisted me in improving ASR quality.

work.name: Université de Genève
work.summary: I joined the EduGame Work Package of the NCCR Evolving Language. The project aimed at leveraging action video games' mechanics to foster reading acquisition in children. I was involved in the design and development of an automated, computerized cognitive and reading assessment battery that was to be used to assess the impact of a gamified attentional control training on executive functions and reading skills. I was also responsible for the implementation of automatic speech recognition solutions in the battery to improve the independence of the children during the verbal tests of the battery. Finally, I was responsible for the processing, analysis and interpretation of the assessment's results.

work.name: EPFL
work.summary: During this research experience, we investigated the extent of the coupling between breathing phase, voluntary motor and mental imagery and readiness potential amplitude. Our results indicated that such a coupling existed in both voluntary motor and mental imagery ocnditions, extending the findings of Park et al. (2020) that shed light on breathing, readiness potential and voluntary motor action coupling.

work.name: Open Mind Innovation
work.summary: The main goal of this internship was to find potential stress biomarkers in the electrogastrogram (EGG) during cognitive load-inducing tasks in VR immersion.

publications.name: Family caregiver perspectives on administering home-based stimulation in patients with mild cognitive impairment
publications.summary: We looked into whether caregivers could effectively deliver tACS to MCI patients at home, concluding that it is a viable approach though it can be demanding on the caregiver's daily life. My role in the project focused on supervising the patients and performing the initial data analysis to determine the system's overall acceptability.

publications.name: Cognitive adaptations for memory deficits in MCI and AD patients: A meta-analysis of EEG microstates
publications.summary: This meta-analysis synthesized the results of 12 experimental studies on EEG microstate differences between AD/MCI patients and healthy age-matched controls. Our findings indicate increased microstate A and decreased microstates C/D in MIC and AD patients, suggesting a possible compensatory recruitment of sensory-related areas to make up for executive and memory deficits.

publications.name: Breathing is coupled with voluntary initiation of mental imagery
publications.summary: In this study, we investigated whether the breathing system is associated with voluntary initiation of mental actions (i.e., motor and visual imagery) which are not accompanied by any overt movement. Our findings suggest breathing-action coupling is involved in more general action preparation processing, regardless of any subsequent motor process.

publications.name: Gut-brain coupling and multilevel physiological response to biofeedback relaxation after a stressful task under virtual reality immersion: A pilot study
publications.summary: Recent studies have demonstrated an electrophysiological coupling between the gastrointestinal tract and the brain (gut-brain axis) under resting-state conditions. As the gut-brain axis plays a key role in individual stress regulation, we aimed to examine modulation of gut-brain coupling through the use of an overwhelming and a relaxing module as a first step toward modeling of the underlying mechanisms.

publications.name: Using commercial ASR solutions to assess reading skills in children: A case report
publications.summary: Reading is an acquired skill that is essential for integrating and participating in today’s society. Yet, becoming literate can be particularly laborious for some children. Identifying reading difficulties early enough is the first, necessary step toward remediation. Here we investigate the opportunities and limitations of integrating commercial, off-the-shelf automatic speech recognition (ASR) services from IBM Watson to ease the administration and evaluation of children’s reading assessment tests in French and Italian.
